rules.title: Move vs Copy classification
rules.statement: A value is a Move type (consuming it invalidates its source, and it cannot be moved while borrowed) iff it owns droppable resources and is not Copy; otherwise it is Copy. Structs/enums with a Drop impl are droppable; primitives, raw pointers, &T, and Copy-impl types are Copy. Classification recurses structurally over tuples, arrays, struct fields, and enum payloads, so an aggregate carrying any Move element (e.g. (String, i64)) is itself Move.

rules.title: &mut T is move, &T is copy
rules.statement: &mut T is a Move type: passing or binding a &mut reference moves the unique mutable borrow. &T is Copy.

rules.title: Bare type parameter moves unless Copy-bounded
rules.statement: Inside a generic body a bare type-parameter T is a Move type unless it carries an explicit `T: Copy` bound; partial moves of fields typed T are tracked accordingly.

rules.title: Drop impl or droppable field makes a type need-drop
rules.statement: A struct needs drop iff it has a Drop impl or has any field that (transitively) needs drop; generic instantiations are matched by their concrete (mono-mangled) name so droppable fields of generic containers are not missed.

rules.title: Affine ownership: move consumes once
rules.statement: A Move variable is consumed on its first use in value position; any subsequent use (whole-value or of an already-moved field) is an error (use-after-move).

rules.title: Shared vs exclusive borrow exclusivity
rules.statement: &T (shared) may be held multiply and blocks moves and &mut of the same place; &mut T (exclusive) permits one at a time and blocks moves and all other borrows of the same place.

rules.title: Two-phase borrows for &mut call arguments
rules.statement: A &mut x taken as a function-call argument is reserved during the rest of argument evaluation and activated at call entry; a reservation does not block concurrent shared reads but does block other mutable borrows.

rules.title: Disjoint field paths borrow independently
rules.statement: Borrows are tracked by dotted field path; disjoint field paths of the same value may be borrowed simultaneously, even mutably. Two borrows conflict iff one path is a prefix of the other (equal included); a whole-value borrow is path "" and conflicts with every field path.

rules.title: Borrow scope: lexical with NLL release
rules.statement: A bound borrow lives in the scope of its holder binding but is released once the holder's last use has passed (non-lexical lifetimes). Call-site borrows (&x in arguments) not bound to a holder are transient and released after the call.

rules.title: Mutation/&mut requires a mut binding
rules.statement: Taking &mut x or assigning to x requires x to be a `let mut` binding; against an immutable binding both are rejected.

rules.title: No returning a reference to a local
rules.statement: A function returning &T or &mut T must not return a reference whose provenance includes a local variable; parameters outlive the call and are safe to borrow from, locals are not.

rules.title: &dyn Trait data half is a borrowed reference
rules.statement: A borrowing trait object (&dyn Trait, non-owning Kind::TraitObject) is treated as a reference kind for dangling-return detection: returning &dyn Trait to a local is rejected; an owning Box<dyn Trait> does not qualify.

rules.title: Reference into a statement-scoped temporary dangles on escape
rules.statement: A reference borrowing into a statement-scoped temporary (a fresh value with no named storage: a literal, struct/tuple/array/enum literal, or call/method/closure-call result, including compiler-materialized `__rtmp_N` receivers) dangles the moment it escapes its enclosing statement (e.g. `let v = make().view();`).

rules.title: Reference provenance tracks param/local origin
rules.statement: Each reference-typed variable tracks the set of function parameters it may alias and whether any path originates from a local; provenance from a global or function return value is treated as safe to return. Provenance merges across branches by union of param-sets and OR of the is_local/is_temp flags.

rules.title: #[borrow_carrying] values are escape-tracked like references
rules.statement: A value of a `#[borrow_carrying]` struct or enum holds a borrow into an arena and is escape-tracked like a reference; returning it escapes the borrow as if returning the bare reference. Borrow-carrying-ness propagates transitively: a struct with an inline field, or an enum with a variant payload, of a (transitively) borrow-carrying type is itself borrow-carrying, as is a container whose generic type-argument is borrow-carrying (e.g. Vec<WAny>).

rules.title: Residency-holder packages are exempt from borrow-carrying
rules.statement: A struct with an Rc/Arc field (a residency-holder / laundered-escape package such as Held<T>/HeldAny) ref-counts the arena alive independent of any local, so it is NOT borrow-carrying and may safely escape — even via its type-arguments. An explicit `#[borrow_carrying]` annotation overrides this auto-exemption.

rules.title: Borrow place: field path with index/deref granularity
rules.statement: The borrowed place of &expr is computed by walking field reads (accumulating a dotted path), index/slice steps (whole-element granularity: prior path components are discarded and the path is the route to the container, no disjointness on the index value), and reference/owning-container derefs (which root the borrow on the deref'd variable). The walk terminates at a variable reference giving the root; `&*r` roots on r.

rules.title: Indexing or dereferencing a raw pointer creates no tracked borrow
rules.statement: Indexing through a raw pointer (p[i], p: *mut/*const T) or dereferencing a raw pointer (*p) is an unsafe raw access that creates no tracked borrow of the base; aliasing safety is the programmer's responsibility inside unsafe (Rust parity).

rules.title: Branch merge unions move state; borrows are scope-local
rules.statement: At control-flow joins, move (Phase-1) state is merged conservatively by union of moved sets; borrows are scope-local (released by scope pop) and do not survive merges. Variables of outer scope moved inside a loop body are dead after the loop.
